authorization: Researcher prioritizes decoding phase transitions and correction thresholds in the continuing Lab 008 study.
question: Can the physical-domain second moment of selector preimage multiplicity be bounded uniformly by a geometric collision or arm-event argument?
claim_boundary: The proved direct inequality reduces positive midpoint Bayes risk to a uniform bound on kappa_L. This contract studies only that selector second moment and retains the full charge record.
alternatives: Represent pairs of majority states mapping to one target as a geometric multi-path or arm event and test whether known critical-percolation estimates make its physical expectation summable.
Average over a registered finite family of path orders or randomized selectors and derive the smallest second-moment bound before choosing a deterministic realization.
Construct a compatible square-lattice family in which selector collisions force kappa_L to diverge on positive physical mass.
planned_steps: Derive an exact paired-state identity for sum_y m_y^2 and classify collision witnesses by path symmetric difference and boundary attachments.
Run the smallest L3/L4 exact matrix needed to test every geometric class and selector-order alternative without extrapolation.
Audit primary arm-event, revealment and switching results against the classified collision events; stop at a uniform theorem, compatible divergence mechanism, or named hypothesis gap.
acceptance_criteria: The paired-state identity exactly replays both extremal-selector second moments at L3/L4.
Every selector comparison uses the same physical majority domains and reports kappa_L before any order is preferred.
Any arm-event bound retains the full external charge record and states whether its exponent or summability is proved for square bond percolation.
The result promotes no size trend or threshold claim from L3/L4 controls.
observed_findings: For every tested selector, sum_y m_y^2 exactly equals A_L plus twice the number of unordered off-diagonal majority-state pairs mapped to one target. Each pair is the symmetric difference of two distinct selected rough-to-rough paths and has even interior degree.

All four path orders use identical majority domains. Shortest-then-lexicographic is best at both controls: kappa_3=11/9 with risk certificate 567/1408, and kappa_4=3113/1605 with certificate 110769075/408027136.

L4 collision pairs include symmetric differences with zero, two, or four odd rough-boundary endpoints and one or two connected components for the shortest selector; other orders reach three components. These are not one standard monotone or alternating-arm event.

Kesten-type arm estimates, triangular-site exact arm exponents, and revealment inequalities do not currently provide a full-charge-conditioned summable bound for every selector-collision class. No positive-mass square-lattice divergence family is constructed.
decision_boundary: The exact collision identity and bounded common-domain order matrix are complete. Shortest-then-lexicographic is the finite winner, but no uniform kappa_L theorem, divergence mechanism, or threshold conclusion follows.
stop_rule: Do not enumerate L5, optimize an unrestricted selector family, fit kappa_L versus size, or infer midpoint noncorrectability. Stop after the bounded collision-class and theorem-hypothesis matrix is complete.
